references.text: Jacob's blessing over Reuben as the firstborn, but who lost his birthright due to his sin. Moses' blessing in Deuteronomy 33:6 asks that the tribe survive despite this history.
Reuben's sin with Bilhah, his father's concubine, which led to the tribe being reduced in significance. Moses' prayer that Reuben may live and not die refers to the tribe's continued existence.
The census of the tribe of Reuben showed 46,500 men. The phrase 'let his men be numbered' in Deuteronomy 33:6 may refer to the size of the tribe.
The second census of the tribe of Reuben. Moses' blessing asks that the tribe continue to exist with a significant number.
The tribe of Reuben settled on the east side of the Jordan. Moses' blessing that they should live and not die relates to their continued existence in this area.
